🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Monday, 2 November 2026

1. 🏠 More than 2.3m UK households face mortgage payment rise in 2027
More than 2.3m UK households coming off fixed-rate deals in 2027 face a sharp rise in payments.

2. 🏥 NHS to introduce what it calls world's largest child early warning system
A national paediatric early warning system, which uses vital signs scoring, is being introduced in A&E departments across England to spot when sick children are dangerously deteriorating, NHS leaders have said.

3. 🔪 'No Place for Knives' campaign launches in London knife crime hotspots
The campaign to deter knife crime is appearing on billboards, in digital advertising and on social media across Westminster and Croydon.

4. 💼 Skilled migrants would boost UK public finances by £115bn, analysis finds
The analysis assumes current rules stay in place.

5. 👑 King to address slavery in Antigua as PM open to possible UK apology
King Charles III will deliver a speech to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting on Tuesday, as he concludes his nine-day Caribbean tour.

6. 🏎️ Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest world champion in F1 history
Antonelli took the Formula 1 title as Max Verstappen won the Mexico City Grand Prix.

7. ⚽ Arsenal win at Anfield for first time since 2012
Arsenal moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League after an end-to-end match, leaving Liverpool frustrated to have taken nothing from the game.

8. 🎻 Teenage violinist Sofia Demetriades wins BBC Young Musician 2026
It was the first all-female final in the competition's 48-year history.

Sources: Guardian, GOV.UK Home Office, The Independent, BBC, BBC Sport. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay. Photos: White House / Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

items.title: More than 2.3m UK households face mortgage payment rise in 2027
items.body: More than 2.3m UK households coming off fixed-rate deals in 2027 face a sharp rise in payments. The Bank of England is widely expected to begin raising interest rates this week.

items.body: The analysis assumes current rules stay in place. The home secretary has faced backlash from within her own party over her migration reforms.
